use_case_summary: Customer building a customer support assistant and internal knowledge search for financial products; needs low-latency interactive chat for customers plus high-throughput embedding/reranking for search. Sensitive to cost but prioritizes tail latency predictability during market events.
latency_slo_details: Customer requires a formal SLO doc: - Non-streaming interactive calls: target p50=60ms, p95=180ms, p99=450ms (client-side inclusive). - Streaming (token-by-token) calls: measured at first-byte and per-token averages; target first-byte p95=120ms, per-token p95 increment <=30ms for short responses. - Measurement alignment: agreed that SLOs will be defined on client-perceived latency (end-to-end), with server-side metrics used for root-cause. Instrumentation plan: client SDK adds X-Client-Sent and X-Client-Recv timestamps; Redwood to supply span names for Console traces and a mapping table. - Sampling & aggregation: production sampling at 1% for full traces, 100% for synthetic canaries; p50/p95/p99 computed on rolling 30d window for alerts, 7d window for immediate rollback. - Streaming vs non-streaming: SLOs split; streaming first-byte and steady-state per-token windows; non-streaming overall response time. - Clock sync: recommend NTP/PTP and include skew tolerance; explicit calibration job in POC. - SLA negotiation: credits for missed monthly p95 targets, escalation path, and a canary-run acceptance test before go-live.
throughput_and_capacity: Requested throughput: sustained 300 req/s, 5m burst 600 req/s. Redwood proposed dedicated pool: 8 x A100-equivalent nodes + 2 hot-standby for failover, autoscale policy for 15% headroom. Batching policy: 20-50ms aggregation window for higher throughput on reranking. Expected cost delta between dedicated vs hosted estimated in pricing deck.
